prev_agent: --- Every time I finish a meaningful coding session — a tricky bug, a feature that took three different approaches before clicking — I think: this would make a useful write-up. The decisions, the dead ends, the thing that finally worked. Stuff that could help another developer. Or just future me. But the write-up never happens. The session ends, the context disappears, and you move on. Code Insights already captures this — every decision, learning, and technique from your AI sessions, structured and sitting in a local database. The gap was just the last mile: turning it into something shareable. When Entire.io shipped their "Dispatch" feature for teams — scoping a repo and generating a narrative of what shipped — it cemented the idea for me. That's the direction. But Code Insights is local-first and single-user, so the right version here isn't a team newsletter from git commits. It's a blog post or LinkedIn update about the decisions you made, the problem you solved, the thing you learned — told in your voice, from your sessions. Today we shipped **Dispatch** as part of Code Insights v4.11.0. Select insights from your sessions, pick a format (Blog or LinkedIn), add a short note about why it matters, and generate. Preview, copy, or download as Markdown. Runs locally on your configured LLM — no cloud, no account. Still early. But it feels like the right thing to build next. Code Insights is free and open source → github.com/melagiri/code-insights --- The problem leads, Entire.io gets a natural nod as the spark that confirmed it, but the origin is clearly your own observation. Want any final tweaks?
